B.Tech · Robotics and Artificial Intelligence

Turn sensor data into controlled motion.

Program a mobile robot to sense and steer, control a robotic arm and use computer vision in moving machines.

Book a campus visit

How a robot acts on what it sees

Robots in warehouses, farms, hospitals and factories have to make decisions in a physical world. A camera gives a machine a view of its surroundings. Software interprets what it sees. Mechanics and control turn that decision into movement.

Mobile robots, arms and vision systems

These projects illustrate the proposed year-by-year progression. Ask admissions for the latest curriculum.

Year 1 Mobile robots

Build robots that detect their surroundings and steer.

Year 2 Robotic arms

Build an arm and control how precisely it moves.

Year 3 Machines that see

Work on computer vision, drones and self-driving platforms.

Year 4 Robots that learn

Train robots using data and simulation, then apply your skills in a supervised work semester.

Motion control, perception and simulation

The proposed curriculum covers programming and algorithms, mechanics and mechatronics, motors and control, embedded systems, kinematics and motion planning, computer vision, machine learning, ROS 2 and simulation.

Where it leads

Explore work in robotics, industrial automation, machine perception, autonomous systems and drone technology. The course also offers a foundation for building a robotics company.

For those who want the detail

The projects progressively combine sensor inputs, motion control and perception. Students use simulation to test behaviours and learn to evaluate those behaviours on a physical system. Individual practical assessments complement team builds.

See how projects and skill tests work

Common questions

How much of the course involves coding?

Programming and algorithms are core skills. You also write software for sensors, controllers, motion planning and machine vision.

Do I need robotics experience to start?

The learning model starts with foundational skills and smaller builds. More complex projects follow as you practise programming, electronics and control.
